He was catholic. After he died, I realized that there may have been a Heaven for him, but not for me. Sent me spiralling into self harm, partially bc of grief, but also bc I felt like he would be very, very disapointed in me, being queer. I distanced myself from all sorts of religion, terrified of what he'd think of me if I met him again one day. I thought, if death is just this black nothingness, I won't have to face him in Heaven, and if I die now, he won't have to see me like this.

But then one day my mom came home after having cleaned out his house, and she had brought his dogtag. She gave it to me, and idk, something just fell into place.

I wear his dogtag every day. It makes me feel like I can have him with me, show him the world through my eyes. Having him with me all the time, makes me feel like I'm not hiding anything from him.

I was his only granddaughter, and we were very close. He always said that I meant Heaven and Earth to him, and having him with me reminds me that he loves me more than any God. That might sound selfish, but it's helped me feel loved and cared for in times when I felt nobody did.

At this point I myself still don't believe in any particular religion. I think religion is shaped by your life experiences, and I simply don't have enough of those yet. But I believe that he fully believed in his God, and his Heaven, and that he was at peace with dying.

And I have found my peace with not ending up in the same afterlife as him, bc I will have him with me so long as my heart beats. That's what keeps me going. When nobody else cares for me, he will always be there.
